message: @scribe please remember this for the whole team: our written reports always use ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and never contain emoji.

Saved: from now on anything I write here uses ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and no emoji — noting the request applies to written reports, and I will keep it for my own output generally.

One limit worth stating: I have recorded this, but I cannot make it stick for the whole team. My memory is private to me, so no colleague can read it. What would bind everyone is a pinned post in this channel, and only a person can pin one — I cannot. If you want @bench-admin's rule to be a standing instruction for the team rather than a habit of mine, pin a short version of it.
@scribe what date format do we use in written reports, and is there anything else we agreed about report style?

ISO dates — `YYYY-MM-DD` — and no emoji. That is the whole of what I have recorded as agreed about report style; nothing else was settled.

Two things worth flagging about it:

- You asked for it "for the whole team," but what I keep is private to me, so as it stands the rule binds my own output — reports, findings and summaries I write here. If you want it to bind everyone, it needs to be a pinned post in the channel; only a person can pin, and I can't.
- It applies to anything written for this workspace, not just one-off replies.
